business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Magazine Publishing and Sponsored Media Placements

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law in Quebec under the Civil Code of Quebec, with federal common-law and statutory overlay).
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied)
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCCA)
Canada-France Tax Convention (1975, as amended by subsequent protocols)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ, arts. 2186 and 2236 et seq. (société en commandite); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, arts. 2, 9, 16, 20, and 21; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and its regulations on client identification, record keeping, beneficial ownership, PEP screening, and sanctions reporting; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each natural-person general partner and each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority in the individual's country of origin, with authentication by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention) for Apostille Contracting States; Consular Legalization for non-Contracting States

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certified registry extract for any corporate general partner organized outside Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the entity's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, depending on origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney and UBO declaration executed by the general partner and all relevant limited partners, appointing Quebec counsel and accepting service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the signatory's jurisdiction, followed by the designated competent authority under the Hague Apostille Convention or Canadian consular official
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; if executed before a Quebec notary, the notarial minute is used directly

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners owning or controlling 25% or more, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian domestic sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, FINTRAC guidance, OFAC SDN List as best practice, and reputable PEP databases. False-positive hits must be documented; actual PEPs trigger enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval; all records retained at least five years under PCMLTFA requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Centre de services en ligne / Register of Enterprises online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name of a Quebec limited partnership must have a French form that complies with the Charter of the French Language and REQ policy. The distinctive element must be transliterated into a phonetically acceptable French spelling where it originates in another Latin-script language; names in non-Latin script must be systematically transliterated into French. The mandatory legal designation is 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; the English designation 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' may be used only as an authorized secondary version.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canada / Québec / federal / provincial / municipal and related sovereign tokens, unless expressly authorized by the competent government body
Banque / bank / trust / insurance, requiring regulatory approval from financial-services authorities
Université / university / collège / école, requiring prior authorization from the competent educational authority
Commission / conseil / ministère / directeur général, implying a public or governmental body
Police / intelligence / sécurité / défense, implying state security functions, restricted without Crown authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ refusal, the notice states the statutory and administrative reasons. An administrative request for review may be filed with REQ within 30 days of the refusal, together with a corrected or alternative French name. If the refusal is maintained, a formal appeal can be filed before the Tribunal administratif du Québec within 60 days of the REQ decision. Any reservation extension must be requested before the initial 90-day window expires; only one extension is normally available unless the request is supported by exceptional circumstances.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this digital-publishing business, provided the virtual office supplies a real physical address in Quebec, is not merely a post-office box, and is capable of receiving service of process and regulatory correspondence. A mail-forwarding-only arrangement will not satisfy REQ legal publicity requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated 5-10% annual probability for an online-only magazine portal with no physical regulated activity; the probability rises to approximately 20-30% if Revenu Quebec identifies payroll, QST/GST, transfer-pricing, or UBO transparency red flags.

Notarized declaration of beneficial ownership and consent to act by general partner and UBOs
Hague Apostille authentication of foreign corporate good-standing and passport copies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization contingency for documents originating in non-Hague Contracting States

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) and Quebec counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus fixed professional fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO file intake, PEP and sanctions screening, and risk assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: International law firm / compliance services provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, Book Fifth, arts. 2236-2244 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 2, 21-26.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) for a Société en Commandite
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a Quebec limited partnership; partners' contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement, and no escrow account is required by statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole general partner hereby adopts and ratifies the Partnership Agreement for CA LP, dated ______, as the constitutional governance document of the limited partnership. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the partnership shall be established at [Canadian Address] in the Province of Quebec, and the principal business is digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements under ISIC 5813. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed General Partner and Chief Compliance Officer, and [Name] is appointed Partnership Secretary and Money Laundering Reporting Officer, each to serve until removed. FINALLY, RESOLVED, that the General Partner and Partnership Secretary are jointly authorized to execute all filings with the Registraire des entreprises and other regulatory authorities to complete statutory formation and licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a secured name search for the proposed limited partnership name. Submit an online request to reserve the name for a period of 90 days; ensure name complies with Quebec civil language requirements under the Charter of the French Language.
required_dossiers: Proof of rights to use the name (if applicable)
Declaration respecting complementary legal designation 'société en commandite'
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name with attestation of distinction and submit a reconsideration request, or appeal to the registr_ Advisory Committee within 45 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement specifying capital contributions, profit-sharing, governance of the general partner, restrictions on limited partners, and dissolution events. Prepare the declaration of registration in the prescribed form listing the general partner, registered office, establishment information, and object of the enterprise.
required_dossiers: Identification and addresses of general partner and all limited partners
Certificate of nationality/domicile of non-resident partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry may require notarized signature of the general partner or corrective amendments; file an amended declaration within 30 days and pay the correction fee to cure any incompleteness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Registration with the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the declaration of registration electronically via the REQ online portal, or in paper by mailing the completed form to the Québec office. Pay the registration fee by credit card or certified payment. Upon acceptance, receive the enterprise identification number (NEQ) and official certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if a representative files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond within 15 days with supplementary declarations or amended documents; the registr_ may issue a formal refusal, subject to judicial review before the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with Revenu Québec for Quebec sales tax (QST), payroll deductions, and corporate/partnership income reporting. Register with CNESST for occupational health and safety, and open a workplace file if employees are hired. Obtain a source deductions number and employer account.
required_dossiers: Identification of the person acting as employer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or incomplete registration may be regularized by filing retroactively with voluntary disclosure; the CNESST provides a cure notice for missing workplace information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Records and Ongoing Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the record book containing the partnership agreement, resolutions, registers of partners, consents, and minutes of partnership meetings. File the initial annual declaration with REQ within the required period and maintain updated records for beneficial ownership information.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For missing annual declarations, file late with penalty; repeated defaults may be stricken from the registry, and reactivation involves a formal reinstatement declaration and payment of arrears.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements are not industrial activities requiring provincial manufacturing or operational licensing in Québec.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license required; applicability of professional authorizations under the Act respecting legal publicity remains in force.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — wholly digital editorial operation, no physical construction or industrial activity; EIA filing not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or solid-waste discharge thresholds apply. Digital content storage must comply with Quebec privacy and data governance standards if cross-border processing is involved.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Commercial lease locations must comply with the Quebec Construction Code and fire safety requirements, including emergency exit inspection and smoke alarm certification; physical workspace clearance is issued by the local fire prevention authority. CNESST registration is mandatory once any employee is engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal GST/HST administration through the Business Number (BN) portal 'My Business Account'; Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administration and registration via the 'Entreprises Québec' portal using the Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ), with joint GST/HST-QST filing through a single combined return administered by Revenu Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Limited Partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ. Step 2: Apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online (BRO), Form RC1, or written application, selecting the GST/HST account; a non-resident general partner or a resident partner must act as the designated representative, and the LP must appoint a Canadian agent for service of process if it carries on business in Quebec without a resident partner. Step 3: Complete QST registration with Revenu Québec (Form LM-1-V thereafter integrated into the BN/NEQ linkage) to obtain a QST number and the 'CléNuméro d'accès' for the Revenu Québec online portal. Step 4: For non-resident partners, file Form RC371 (Non-Resident Partnership Information Return) and ensure each partner's Canadian residency status is documented, as the LP itself is not an income tax payer but must file an information return (Form T5013) and allocate income to partners. Effective registration dates follow the small-supplier threshold rules; voluntary registration is permitted once a Canadian permanent establishment or taxable supply activity exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The Quebec Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian federal and Quebec income tax purposes; income, losses, and tax credits flow through to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement and the Income Tax Act (Canada) (ITA) and the Taxation Act (Quebec). For GST/HST and QST, however, the partnership is treated as a separate 'person' required to register, collect, and remit tax in its own name. A limited partner's deductible loss is restricted to the adjusted cost base of the partnership interest (at-risk rules), and the partnership must use a calendar-year fiscal period unless an election is made to use a different business fiscal period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No IRS-style 'check-the-box' election exists in Canada; entity classification is determined by statute (LP = transparent). Available elections include: (i) partnership fiscal period election under subsection 249.1(4) ITA permitting a non-calendar-year business period where all partners are non-residents or, in narrowly defined cases, for Canadian resident partners; (ii) GST/HST joint election under section 273 ETA to treat closely related corporations/partnerships as a single person for registration and compliance; (iii) GST/HST quick method election and annual remittance election to simplify filing; (iv) election under section 216 ITA for non-resident partners earning Canadian rental income from the partnership; (v) Quebec parallel elections under the Taxation Act and the QST Act, including the election to align QST registration with GST registration; and (vi) the voluntary disclosure election to the CRA and Revenu Québec to correct past filing positions before a compliance action begins.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) combined with Quebec Sales Tax (QST) — a value-added tax (VAT) system administered in Quebec through a single GST/HST-QST combined return filed with Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the small-supplier threshold for both GST/HST (Excise Tax Act, section 240) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax Act, section 27), measured on the worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports and certain financial services) of the partnership together with associates, over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; registration becomes mandatory the moment the threshold is exceeded, with an effective date at that time or earlier upon request.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a mandatory real-time continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance regime, government digital stamping, or QR-code clearance for e-invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted without prior fiscal authorization, provided the invoice contains all prescribed information under the Excise Tax Act (sections 3, 169, 223) and the QST Act (sections 26–30), including vendor name and BN, recipient name, date of supply, consideration, GST/QST rates and amounts, and a description of the digital magazine portal services. Taxpayers must retain electronic records in a readable, auditable format accessible to the CRA and Revenu Québec on request; there is no API-based fiscal clearance, but payment data from Stripe and AdSense must be reconciled against invoice-level transaction logs to support zero-rating claims and input tax credit claims, and any large-volume e-invoicing system should maintain a tamper-evident audit trail to withstand audit scrutiny.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of digital magazine content, subscriptions, and sponsored advertising placements are eligible for the 0% export rate when supplied to a non-resident person (not an individual who is present in Canada, and not a registrant carrying on business in Canada) under sections 5 and 7 of Part V, Schedule VI ETA (services to non-residents and advertising services, respectively), and under the mirror provisions of the QST Act (Schedule IV, sections 5 and 7). The portal must demonstrably establish that: (i) the recipient is a non-resident, (ii) the digital property is delivered electronically to a foreign IP address or foreign-based account, (iii) the contract is negotiated and executed abroad, and (iv) payment is received from a foreign financial institution. For corporate subscribers, a completed and signed form of the CRA prescribed 'Exports — Non-Resident Status Certificate' (or equivalent documentary evidence, such as a certificate of incorporation, tax residency certificate, or foreign VAT number) should be retained. Advertising services supplied to a non-resident advertiser are zero-rated even if the advertisement is intended to be directed at a Canadian audience, provided the 'directly in connection with real property in Canada or a service rendered in respect of the property' exceptions do not apply; periodic legal review of the supply chain is required to confirm that no supply of a Canadian advertising agency's services in Canada or any supply made to a Canadian resident is bundled with the zero-rated supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / CAED) — required only for physical shipments of printed magazines or promotional materials crossing the Canadian border; electronically delivered digital content falls outside the customs declaration requirement but must be evidenced by log files and delivery records
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill — mandatory for any physical export shipment to substantiate the goods leaving Canada and to match with the customs declaration and the commercial invoice

Inward Remittance Certificate — a bank-issued certificate, SWIFT MT103, or foreign currency credit advice evidencing receipt of payment in Canadian dollars or convertible foreign currency from the non-resident counterparty, to be matched to each zero-rated export invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec aggressively audit digital exporters; where zero-rating substantiation is incomplete, both authorities may reassess the entire revenue stream as taxable at 14.975% (GST/QST), deny corresponding input tax credits, and re-characterize the amounts for income tax, resulting in compound statutory interest on the unpaid balances from the original filing due date. Penalties include: (i) late-filing and late-remittance penalties of 5% of the amount owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (ETA sections 280 and 284; QTA parallel rules); (ii) gross negligence penalties of up to 25% of the net tax misstated for GST/HST and up to 50% for income tax false statements; (iii) false statements or omissions penalties of up to CAD 25,000 per person under ETA section 285.1; (iv) Québec administrative monetary penalties under the Tax Administration Act; and (v) personal liability of directors of the corporate general partner for unremitted GST/QST and payroll amounts under ETA section 323 and QTA section 31, without the due-diligence defence applying where the director knew of the deficiency. Retrospective clawbacks generally extend four years from the date of the original assessment (unlimited in cases of misrepresentation or fraud), and the Voluntary Disclosures Program (CRA) and the Québec Voluntary Disclosure Program may mitigate penalties, but not interest, if a qualifying voluntary disclosure is filed before any audit notification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) regulates federally chartered banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers money laundering reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility for both current and capital accounts under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. There are no foreign exchange controls or restrictions on profit remittance. Non-resident partners of a Canadian limited partnership are subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax on allocated Canadian-source income under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada), with treaty relief available under the Canada–US Tax Treaty and other applicable treaties. No prior governmental approval is required for dividend/distribution remittances, only tax compliance through Form NR4 and Form NR424.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio for export or advertising revenue proceeds in Canada. Export receipts may be retained in any currency in a domestic or foreign bank account, and no repatriation deadline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account with cross-border treasury package

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury clearing rail. Offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are not recognized as deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act (Canada). They may operate only as money service businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC, but they cannot hold wrapped Canadian deposits or provide CDIC insurance. The LP may use an EMI for collection (e.g., Stripe, AdSense payouts), but funds must be swept into a Canadian tier-1 bank account for statutory and tax compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for Canadian limited partnerships when the general partner is a Canadian resident legal entity. No physical director appearance is required; standard onboarding utilises video conferencing for KYC interviews if the partnership has non-resident limited partners or aggregate revenues above CAD 1 million. For lower-risk structures, entirely remote onboarding is available at RBC, TD, and BMO. The bank requires a certified copy of the Quebec Enterprise Registrar (Registraire des entreprises) certificate of registration, partners' register, and a valid partnership agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners with >25% ownership interest, especially from uncooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full legal name, residential address, source of wealth, source of funds, and tax identification number for each limited partner; notarized passport pages; proprietary beneficial ownership attestation; organizational chart showing every owner up to the ultimate natural person; evidence of the Canadian general partner's substantive management functions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket digital advertising receipts (AdSense/ Stripe) creating fragmented transaction patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a signed business plan confirming digital magazine operations, sample executed advertising contracts, processing history from Stripe/AdSense dashboard, and a wire-level audit trail for all cross-border settlement receipts; maintain a reconciliation ledger linking each deposit to a specific publication or sponsorship invoice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward capital contributions from non-bank financial intermediaries or EMI corporate credit cards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a capital contribution certificate, the bank statement of the sending institution (where available), an anti-money laundering (AML) source-of-funds declaration certified by a qualified Canadian accountant, and confirmation that no third-party lending or currency exchange is embedded in the contribution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the Quebec limited partnership must route via the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers. Use SWIFT purpose code 'BEQU' (capital payment) or 'PCAP' (capital contribution) for non-resident inbound; for distributions from digital advertising, use the commercial purpose code 'ADV' (advertising revenue). Funds must reference the LP's Business Number (BN) and the bank's internal customer ID. Verification requires a signed contribution agreement, a board or general partner resolution approving the injection, and a source-of-funds report from the remitting institution. For amounts exceeding CAD 100,000, the bank will file a Large Cash Transaction Report (LCTR) equivalent under FINTRAC Program Requirements and may request an enhanced due diligence form.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for digital magazine royalties, content licensing, and freelance contributors shall be executed via SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for cross-border wire payments, or through Canadian EFT/ACH for domestic payments. For high-value transactions above CAD 50,000, use the Real-Time Rail (RTR) through Payments Canada where applicable. International content provider contracts above CAD 250,000 may optionally use a commercial letter of credit (LC), but given the low physical goods exposure of ISIC 5813, a telegraphic transfer (T/T) with invoice matching is the standard rail. All outbound payments must be pre-screened against the Canadian consolidated sanctions list (Canada's Autonomous Sanctions List) and the United Nations Security Council resolutions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/CAD forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank (maturity up to 12 months, non-deliverable settlements allowed for corporate counterparties).
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on currencies without active onshore deliverability (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) executed through a resident Canadian dealer with ISDA Master Agreement.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD) for long-term treasury matching interest and principal cash flows between advertising revenue (USD) and operating expenses (CAD).
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put) on CAD/USD to cap adverse rate movements without premium amortisation, subject to the LP's partnership investment policy and general partner authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) of the Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the entity's registration date; must be filed every 12 months without regard to fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to fine between CAD 200 and CAD 2,000; persistent default triggers an administrative notice from the REQ and may result in cancellation or strike-off of the LP's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than five months after each fiscal period end; for a calendar-year digital publishing portal, due on or before March 30 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty under Income Tax Act subsection 162(7) applies; recurring non-filing may trigger additional penalties and forced electronic filing or compliance action by the CRA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec Partnership Information Return (Relevé no. 126 / accompanying declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal period end date plus five months; calendar-year partnerships must file by March 30/31 of the following year as prescribed by Revenu Québec.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest are assessed under the Taxation Act; continued default can lead to escalated collection measures and prosecution in aggravated cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is imposed on an ordinary Québec limited partnership solely under the Civil Code of Québec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An independent audit becomes mandatory if the LP is a reporting issuer under securities law or is otherwise required by National Instrument 51-102 to file audited financial statements; if it has gross revenue above CAD 10,000,000 and total assets above CAD 5,000,000 under the audit thresholds applicable to non-public enterprises, or if the partnership agreement, lender, regulator, or a governing contractual mandate requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises or, for private enterprises and many limited partnerships, Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Financial records must support the annual declaration and any federal/Quebec tax information returns.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not impose a separate annual UBO declaration for limited partnerships. The LP's annual declaration to the REQ must contain current partner and general partner information; any transfer of a partnership interest or change in partner identity, contribution, or address must be declared with the REQ within 15 days. The LP must also maintain accurate internal records of all partners, their contributions, profit-sharing percentages, and any control or ownership changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 12,000 when an audit is contractually or regulatorily required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal and provincial corporate rate; partnership is pass-through)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Quebec multimedia tax credit (up to 30% on eligible labour), SR&ED tax credit (up to 25% on eligible R&D), and small business deduction for eligible corporate partners

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Canada Revenue Agency) and RL-15 (Revenu Québec); filed via CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec's CLIC system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., if year-end Dec 31, due May 31)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership business income (loss) for the fiscal period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to non-resident partners based on partnership agreement; report on T5013 and RL-15
Report capital gains allocated to non-resident partners; subject to Part XIII withholding on distributions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership deductions (e.g., CCA, interest, administrative expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure deductions are properly allocated and substantiated; non-resident partners must receive supporting schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership foreign income and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign-source income and claim foreign tax credits on partner-level returns

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership expenses for tax credits (e.g., SRCD, multimedia credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate eligible expenses to partners; non-resident partners may claim credits if treaty allows

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $100 per day up to $2,500 for T5013; additional penalties for failure to provide information; Quebec: similar daily penalties up to $2,500 plus interest

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on distributions to non-resident partners (Part XIII withholding tax)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partners must submit Form NR301 (Canada) or equivalent to claim treaty relief; provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from their home jurisdiction; file with CRA before or at time of distribution to reduce withholding rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 25% for royalties and interest; treaty rates may reduce to 10% (royalties) or 0% (interest) under Canada's tax treaties (e.g., US, UK)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 (total value of transactions with non-residents in a fiscal year)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) but applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles; partnerships must demonstrate real business activity and commercial rationale

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or deliberate misreporting of partnership allocations to non-resident partners
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act (s. 239); fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties up to 50% of understated tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they authorized or acquiesced to the evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may apply

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Partnership lacks real economic substance, no employees, no physical presence, or is used solely to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under GAAR; denial of treaty benefits; penalties up to 25% of the tax benefit; potential criminal charges for fraudulent schemes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may be jointly and severally liable for corporate taxes and penalties if they authorized or participated in the sham arrangement; travel bans and extradition possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a money services business, inadequate record-keeping, or suspicious transaction reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 for individuals and CAD 2,000,000 for entities; criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally liable for AML violations if they knowingly failed to implement compliance programs; travel bans and seizure of assets may occur
